title: Riverbend Proof-of-Value Brief
body:
Executive summary:

This brief captures the scope, success criteria, and delivery plan for a 6-week proof-of-value (PoV) with Riverbend Retail. Objective is to demonstrate a 20-30% reduction in average time-to-answer for customer support ticket triage and a 2x increase in relevant suggested answers surfaced by the assistant, without exceeding a $0.018/token cost baseline for hosted inference.

Context and customer problem:
- Riverbend runs an omnichannel support stack (Zendesk + internal ticketing). They want to experiment with an LLM-powered triage assistant that:
  - automatically suggests priority, category, and 1–2 candidate responses,
  - extracts structured entities for downstream routing (order id, sku, store id), and
  - surfaces model confidence so agents can trust suggestions.
- Constraints: PII in tickets (names, partial order ids), VPC requirement for production, and strict SLA for 99th percentile latency in the UI (<350ms ideally).

PoV goals (what success looks like):
1) Business goal: Reduce median agent handle time for triaged tickets by >= 20% in the pilot cohort (support team of 12 agents).
2) Quality goal: Achieve at least 75% precision on extracted entities and 70% top-1 suggestion acceptance rate by agents in live validation sessions.
3) Performance goal: 95th percentile model response latency <= 450ms for typical 80-token responses during target load (50 concurrent requests).
4) Cost target: End-to-end inference cost <= $0.018/token (hosted Redwood API, including caching benefits).
5) Compliance goal: No PII persisted outside Riverbend systems; all logs scrubbed per their data retention policy.

Acceptance criteria (hard pass/fail checks):
- Integration: Successful end-to-end webhook flow from Zendesk sandbox to Redwood hosted inference and back, verified with 100 sample tickets. (PASS if >= 100/100 transactions return structured output within 5xx budget).
- Entity extraction: On evaluation set of 500 withheld tickets, entity precision >= 75% and recall >= 60%.
- Agent validation: In a 2-week live trial with 12 agents, >= 70% of suggested replies are accepted/used (measured by agent action).
- Safety/compliance: No raw ticket text stored in Redwood hosted logs; any debug artifacts must be sanitized and approved by Riverbend security.

Measurement plan and datasets:
- Baseline: Capture 2 weeks of agent handle-time and suggestion acceptance history (if available) before the PoV start.
- Eval set: 500 representative anonymized tickets covering returns, order status, and refunds. Annotate for entities and canonical replies.
- Live telemetry: Use Redwood Console tracing + Riverbend event webhook to record latency, acceptance, and per-token costs.
- Statistical checks: Use bootstrap sampling for confidence intervals on acceptance rate and handle time changes.

Technical scope and deliverables:
- Week 0: Workshop + environment setup (create API keys, sandbox Zendesk integration, access to sample dataset).
- Week 1: Baseline ingestion + quickstart pipeline (validate sample flow, smoke tests).
- Week 2–3: Model selector + prompt engineering cycle; deliver 3 prompt variants and a recommended model and batching config.
- Week 4: Live agent pilot (12 agents) with daily quality review sessions; iterate prompts and fallback handling.
- Week 5: Final measurement window + cost/latency tuning (quantization suggestion or cache rules if needed).
- Week 6: Wrap-up, acceptance sign-off, and handoff plan to Riverbend platform team.

Roles & responsibilities:
- Redwood Solutions Lead: Ava Chen — PoV owner, weekly status, workshop facilitation.
- Redwood Eng Lead: Mateo Ruiz — integration hooks, performance tuning, console dashboards.
- Riverbend Product Owner: Priya Desai — access to ticket datasets, agent scheduling, acceptance sign-off.
- Riverbend Engineer: Mark Taylor — Zendesk sandbox admin, routing changes.
- QA/Analyst: Liam O'Neill — constructs evaluation set, runs metrics.

Technical prerequisites & checklist (pre-work):
- Riverbend provides a sandbox Zendesk org + 500 anonymized sample tickets (by D-3).
- Network: If we demo hosted integration, open outbound to api.redwood.ai on 443 from Riverbend sandbox. If they require private deployment we will scope separately (out of band).
- Credentials: Riverbend creates a scoped API key for PoV (ephemeral, rotate after PoV).
- Data handling: Provide PI redaction rules and retention window; sign the PoV data processing addendum.

Observability and evaluation hooks:
- Redwood Console: per-request latency, per-route token counts, error traces.
- Custom metrics: acceptance_rate, median_handle_time, entity_precision_by_type.
- Alerts: 5xx spike > 1% for 10m, latency p95 > 600ms, downstream webhook failures > 0.5% of requests.

Security and compliance notes:
- No PII should be logged; if debug logs are required they will be redacted and shared over S3 with KMS encryption.
- If Riverbend requires Private deployment, scope will include VPC peering and KMS integration — this is out of PoV scope but must be discussed before Week 2.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Sample tickets are not representative -> Mitigation: Expand evaluation set to 1,000 tickets and stratify by ticket type.
- Risk: Agent adoption lower than expected -> Mitigation: shorter feedback loop, daily huddles, and tweak suggestion threshold.
- Risk: Latency spikes under load -> Mitigation: adjust batching window, enable prefix caching for repeated queries, fallback to lightweight model for 95th percentile.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we have an existing metric for agent acceptance that Riverbend currently tracks? (Priya to confirm)
- Will Riverbend allow us to mask PII client-side or prefer Redwood to handle redaction?
- Approval needed: Legal sign-off on PoV DPA by 2025-10-10.

Workshop agenda (Week 0, 90min):
- 00–10m: Introductions, success recap, constraints alignment.
- 10–30m: Review sample ticket types + annotated examples.
- 30–55m: Integration walkthrough (Zendesk events -> Redwood API -> backfill).
- 55–70m: Latency & cost tradeoffs primer (batching, cache, quantization).
- 70–85m: Acceptance criteria and measurement plan finalization.
- 85–90m: Next steps + immediate actions.

Evaluation artifacts to deliver at end of PoV:
- Dashboard snapshot (latency, cost, usage), annotated evaluation report (entity precision/recall, acceptance rates), recommended production configuration with estimated monthly cost, and an optional private deployment checklist.

Post-PoV transition and options:
- If goals met: propose 90-day pilot (Dedicated capacity) with SLAs and VPC onboarding checklist.
- If partly met: recommend target experiments (prompt sets, training small retrieval augmentation) and a narrowing scope pilot.
- If not met: conduct root-cause analysis and decide on extended experiment or close PoV.

Notes to self (informal):
- Bring a short demo script with 6 diverse ticket examples.
- Confirm Redwood Console view access for Riverbend analytics team.
- Prepare a fallback policy doc describing model swap + routing logic.

Appendix: sample prompts and evaluation rubric (short):
- Prompt v1 (concise): "Given the ticket below, extract order_id, sku, and suggested short response (<=50 tokens). Provide confidence score."
- Rubric example: Suggested response accepted = agent clicks "use suggestion" within 60s. Entity extraction correct = all labeled entities match.

-- End of brief --

Redwood contacts: Ava Chen (ava@redwood.ai), Mateo Ruiz (mateo@redwood.ai).
_note: File created as a working PoV brief for solutions engineering; contains informal notes, open questions, and measurable acceptance criteria.
